info.title: RosterParser public API
info.description:
Public endpoints of RosterParser: read a crew roster (image, PDF, CSV, Excel, text) into rows, turn rows into an iCalendar file, look up airports with their weather, and compute the night time of a flight.

**Base URL**: the host serving this page (all paths start with `/api`).

**Authentication**: an API key. Sign up on `/signup`, make a key on `/account`, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer rp_...` (or `X-API-Key: rp_...`). Without a key the API answers `401`; the pages of this site use it without one. Click **Authorize** above to try the endpoints with your key. The administration endpoints (labels, benchmarks, models) are not part of this API.

**Formats**: JSON in and out (UTF-8) unless stated; uploads are `multipart/form-data`. Times are ISO 8601; roster times keep the roster's notation (`HH:MM Z` = UTC, `L` / `LB` = local).

**Errors**: a non-2xx status with `{ "error": "message" }`. Messages are English by default; send the header `X-UI-Lang: vi` (or the cookie `lang=vi`) for Vietnamese.

**Limits**: each account has a plan (Free: 1,000 requests and 50 files read a day; Pro: 20,000 and 2,000), counted from 00:00 UTC; reading a roster or an ACARS picture counts as a file read. Every answer has `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reads-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix time); past a limit the API answers `429` with `Retry-After` (seconds). Any origin may call the API from a browser (CORS); cookies are not used then. uploads up to 10 MB. Roster reading uses one OCR server for everyone: requests queue, and `503` with `busy: true` means the queue is full, retry after a few seconds. Weather is cached for 30 minutes per airport.

**Privacy**: `POST /api/roster/upload` only reads the file: it is deleted right after and nothing is kept. A roster is kept only when you send it with `POST /api/roster/suggestions` (a correction suggestion): the administrators then use it to improve the model, or delete it.

post.description:
Reads a crew roster into its two tables, "Published roster" and "Rest of this roster is planned", with the AI model (as on /roster). One endpoint for every file type; the server picks the reader from the file:

| File | How it is read | `readMode` |
|---|---|---|
| JPG, PNG, BMP, JFIF (eCrew screenshot) | OCR (PaddleOCR) + AI model | `ocr-image` |
| PDF with a text layer (duty plan, schedule report) | its text + AI model | `text` |
| PDF without a text layer, duty plan | OCR + parser (`source: parser`) | `ocr` |
| PDF without a text layer, roster screen printed to PDF | pages OCRed as one roster image + AI model | `ocr-image` |
| CSV, XLS, XLSX, TXT | its cells / text + AI model | `text` |

Images give the columns date, day, duty, dep, begin, end, arr; other files can add more (see RosterRow). Takes from about one second to a minute depending on the queue. The file is only read: it is deleted right after. To send it to the administrators because the rows are wrong, use `POST /api/roster/corrections` (with the rows corrected) or `POST /api/roster/suggestions` (a report: what is wrong).

file.description: JPG, PNG, BMP, JFIF, PDF, CSV, XLS, XLSX or TXT, up to 10 MB

parameters.description: `1` adds `previewHtml` for CSV / Excel / TXT files

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: `model` (default): the AI model; `parser`: the rule-based parser instead (as /roster "Try to parse" does while correcting a reading)

post.description: The rows read from a roster are wrong? Send the roster file to the administrators, with an optional email address (to get an answer when it is handled), note and the rows that were read. They check it and label it (the file then becomes training data for the model) or dismiss it (the file is deleted). This is the only call that keeps a roster on the server.

file.description: The roster: JPG, PNG, BMP, JFIF, PDF, CSV, XLS, XLSX or TXT, up to 10 MB

email.description: Where the administrators answer when they have handled it (optional; `400` when it is not an email address)

413.description: The file is larger than 10 MB

x-codeSamples.source: curl -F file=@roster.png -F email=crew@example.com -F "note=12 Mar: the duty is OS 769" http://localhost:3000/api/roster/suggestions

post.description: The rows read from a roster were wrong and you corrected them? Send the roster file with the rows as they should be. The file joins the training data with these rows as its label, waiting for an administrator to review them (they are not used to train the model before that). For a roster you cannot correct yourself, use `POST /api/roster/suggestions`.

file.description: The roster: JPG, PNG, BMP, JFIF, PDF, CSV, XLS, XLSX or TXT, up to 10 MB

rows.description: JSON `{ "published": [RosterRow], "planned": [RosterRow] }`: the rows as they should be (not both empty)

period.description: The roster's period, as `POST /api/roster/upload` gave it (optional, e.g. `01Mar25 - 31Mar25`)

post.description: Reads a photo or screenshot of the cockpit's ACARS / AOC OOOI page (OOOI STATUS, FLT LOG, FLIGHT TIMES...) with OCR (PaddleOCR) and the AI model, as on /acars: flight number, date, departure and destination, OUT, OFF, ON, IN, and the flight and block times. The picture is only read: it is deleted right after.

post.description: Turns rows (as returned by the Roster endpoints) into iCalendar events: a check-in .. check-out (C/I .. C/O) becomes one duty event with its flights, sims and hotel inside it (RELATED-TO the duty); a hotel lasts from the event before it to the event after it; rows without times are all-day; `Z` times are UTC, local times are floating; Planned rows are TENTATIVE. Rows whose date cannot be read are skipped.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `json` returns the calendar inside JSON with the counts, instead of the file

200.description: The calendar file (`Content-Disposition: attachment`; headers `X-Events` and `X-Skipped-Rows` give the counts), or JSON with `format=json`

post.summary: Routes of rosters on a world map
post.description:
The flights of one or more rosters as routes on a world map, as /route-map draws them: one route per airport pair, along the great circle, one colour per roster. Rosters can be given as roster rows, as an .ics text or as a list of flights.

**Showing the map.** The answer's `viewUrl` opens `/route-map` with the routes drawn (nothing is kept on the server: the routes are in the link). The link can also be built by hand:

`/route-map?r=<name>|<#color>|<DEP-ARR[*count]>,<DEP-ARR>...&r=...`

one `r` per roster, e.g. `/route-map?r=Jan|%23c0392b|VIE-HAN*2,HAN-VIE*2,VIE-JFK`. Options: `embed=1` (only the map and its legend, for an iframe), `view=globe` (the globe instead of the flat map), `table=0` (no route table).

`?format=geojson` answers a GeoJSON FeatureCollection instead: one LineString per route and roster (properties: from, to, roster, color, flights, distanceKm) and one Point per airport.

rows.summary: Roster rows (one roster at the top level)

400.description: Nothing to draw, or a bad input

example.error: rosters[0].flights[0]: dep and arr must be airport codes

get.summary: Search airports, or look up several codes
get.description:
With `q`: airports whose code is exactly `q` (IATA, ICAO, FAA, GPS, local, ident or WMO) come first, then those whose name, city, region or country contain every word of `q` (accents ignored); bigger airports with scheduled service first.

With `codes`: a map from each code that is an airport to that airport (codes that are not airports are left out). Useful to annotate roster rows.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Code or text, at least 2 characters for a text search

parameters.name: codes
parameters.description: Comma-separated codes (up to 50); takes precedence over `q`

200.description: Search results (`q`) or a code map (`codes`)

503.description: The airport list has not been built on this server (`npm run airports:update`)

get.description: The airport for an IATA, ICAO, FAA, GPS, local, OurAirports ident or WMO code (tried in that order; IATA first, so `VIE` is Vienna). `matchedBy` says which code matched; `others` lists other airports using the same code. Use `icao` as the airport's id: a WMO number identifies a weather station, not the airport.

get.summary: Current weather and a 7-day forecast at an airport
get.description: From Open-Meteo at the airport's coordinates, in the airport's local time. Wind in knots, direction in degrees the wind comes from. Cached 30 minutes per airport. For reference only, not a substitute for METAR / TAF.

502.description: The forecast service did not answer

post.description: The aircraft flies the great circle from `dep` to `arr` at a constant speed between off-block and on-block; the sun's altitude is taken at its position (SunCalc), and each day / night edge is found to the second. Night = the sun below −6° (`civil`: end of evening to beginning of morning civil twilight, ICAO Annex 1 / EASA / FAA) below −0.833° (`sunset`: sunset to sunrise) or below −12° (`nautical`: end of evening to beginning of morning nautical twilight), or by fixed hours (`fixed`: before `sunrise` and from `sunset` on, default 06:00 / 18:00 local time at the aircraft, i.e. the mean solar time of its longitude). Minutes are rounded; `nightMinutes + dayMinutes = blockMinutes`.

200.description: Night, day and block time with the day / night segments

AirportCode.name: code
AirportCode.description: IATA, ICAO, FAA, GPS, local, ident or WMO code (case-insensitive)

Error.description: The file could not be read

Unauthorized.description: No API key, or a key that is not valid (revoked, made up).

example.error: An API key is needed: sign up on /signup, then make a key on /account

TooManyRequests.description: Past the plan's limit of the day (`kind`: `requests` or `reads`). Try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the limit starts again

error.description: What went wrong (English, or Vietnamese with the cookie lang=vi)

busy.description: Only on 503: the OCR queue is full

RosterRow.description: One roster row, values as printed in the roster. Images only give date, day, duty, dep, begin, end, arr; text files may give all.

duty.description: Flight number or activity (C/I, C/O, SBY, OFF, SIM, HT/H1 = hotel, ...)

begin.description: `HH:MM Z` = UTC, `L`/`LB` = local; `A`/`E` prefix = actual/estimated; `+1` = next day

takeoff.description: Takeoff (wheels-off) time, same form as `begin`; empty when the file has none

landing.description: Landing (touchdown) time, same form as `begin`; empty when the file has none

planned.description: "Rest of this roster is planned" table

id.description: OurAirports ident (the ICAO code when there is one)

icao.description: ICAO code: unique, use it as the airport id

local.description: Local code given by the country (outside the US)

wmo.description: WMO number of the weather station at the airport (NOAA ISD); not an airport id

others.description: Other airports using the same code

windDir.description: Degrees, where the wind comes from

sunAltitudeLimit.description: The sun altitude night starts below; null with rule fixed

sunrise.description: rule fixed only: the sunrise used, HH:MM local

sunset.description: rule fixed only: the sunset used, HH:MM local

fileName.description: The uploaded file name (the file itself is not kept)

readMode.description: How the file was read (see the table above)

source.description: `parser` only for an image-only duty-plan PDF, which the model cannot read yet

notices.description: Notes about how the file was read

previewHtml.description: With `?preview=1`, for CSV / XLS / XLSX / TXT: the file as an HTML page (a table or text), to show next to the rows

off.description: Off-block time, ISO 8601 (UTC: end with Z)

on.description: On-block time, ISO 8601; at most 24 h after `off`

rule.description: civil: sun below −6°; nautical: below −12°; sunset: below −0.833°; fixed: night outside sunrise..sunset local time at the aircraft (local mean time of its longitude: UTC + 4 min per degree east)

track.description: true adds the flight track (about 300 points) with the sun altitude at each

sunrise.description: rule fixed: local time the day starts

sunset.description: rule fixed: local time the night starts

AcarsFields.description: What an ACARS OOOI page shows. Times as HH:MM as printed (ACARS prints UTC); a field the picture does not show (or the model could not read) is an empty string.

flt.description: Flight number (FLIGHT NO / FLT ID / CALLSIGN)

date.description: As much of the date as the page prints: "11 Nov 25" (11NOV25, 11/11/25), "28 May" (28/MAY), or only the day, "14" (QFA0057/14)

ms.description: Time taken on the server, in milliseconds

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; only used by the month filter

planned.description: A planned flight (left out with includePlanned: false)

RouteMapRoster.description: One roster, with its flights given in any of three ways (they add up). A row or event is a flight when it goes from one airport to another and its duty is a flight number (has a digit) or empty: ground duties such as "GT LTN → STC" are left out.

color.description: Its colour on the map (#rrggbb); a palette colour when left out

published.description: Roster rows, as POST /api/roster/upload gives them

ics.description: An iCalendar text, as POST /api/calendar/export gives it

RouteMapRequest.description: Several rosters in "rosters", or the fields of one roster at the top level.

month.description: Only the flights of this month (YYYY-MM)

includePlanned.description: false: leave the Planned rows / tentative events out

distanceKm.description: Sum of the flights' great-circle distances

routes.description: One per airport pair (both directions together), busiest first

unknown.description: Airport codes not found (their flights are not on the map)

viewUrl.description: Opens /route-map with these routes. Add &embed=1 to show only the map (for an iframe), &view=globe for the globe, &table=0 without the route table.

status.description: The file is in the data, its label waiting for an administrator

bearerKey.description: Your API key (make one on /account): `Authorization: Bearer rp_...`

apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same key in an `X-API-Key` header.
